diagnostic_tracker.title: Shape Safari — Day 1 Diagnostic Checklist
diagnostic_tracker.when_used: During Lesson 1, while children are at the 2D shape sorting and identification stations.
diagnostic_tracker.usage_notes: Walk between pairs during the partner sort. For each child, tick the columns where you see clear evidence; leave blank if not yet observed (rather than marking 'no'). The 'Finds classroom examples' column is the key signal for which children have transferred shape vocabulary into the world — these can be challenged in Lessons 2-5. Children with blanks across all three skill columns may need a small-group re-loop on Lesson 1 before continuing.
diagnostic_tracker.layout_description: One letter page, portrait orientation. Title at the top, expectation focus (A9.1) in a small box below. A date field and class label in the header row. The body is a table with one column for student names (left, ~1.5in wide), three narrow tick columns (~0.9in each) labelled with the column names, and a Notes column on the right (~2in wide). Approximately 24 blank student rows so the page accommodates a typical Ontario K class.

formative_trackers.title: Shape Safari — Lesson 2 Formative Tracker (3D Shapes)
formative_trackers.when_used: During Lesson 2, while children are at the 3D shape stations identifying and comparing shapes.
formative_trackers.usage_notes: Stop at each pair. Ask 'What shape is this? Is it 2D or 3D? How do you know?' to elicit the third column. Tick when you see clear evidence; leave blank if not observed. The 'Distinguishes 2D and 3D' column is the deepest signal — children who can articulate 'flat vs solid' have crossed the conceptual threshold for the rest of the unit.

formative_trackers.title: Shape Safari — Lesson 3 Formative Tracker (Position Words)
formative_trackers.when_used: During Lesson 3, while pairs are placing animals on the safari map using position cards.
formative_trackers.usage_notes: Stop at each pair. Ask 'Where is the lion? Where is the elephant?' to elicit position words. Tick when you see clear evidence. The 'Uses 5+ position words' column is the precision signal — a child who only uses 'over' for everything is not yet there. The 'Places objects' column captures the productive use (the child can take a position-word direction and act on it correctly).

formative_trackers.title: Shape Safari — Lesson 4 Formative Tracker (Compose and Decompose)
formative_trackers.when_used: During Lesson 4, while pairs are at the compose, decompose, and 3D-build stations.
formative_trackers.usage_notes: These three columns are deliberately separated by skill because they have different difficulties: composing a target from pattern blocks is easiest; decomposing a bigger shape with internal lines is harder; building a 3D structure that names its component shapes is hardest. A child solid on compose but blank on the others is on track for the typical K trajectory. Use this tracker to identify children who are ready for the capstone (3 ticks) versus those who need a 1:1 conference before Lesson 5.

summative_rubric.title: Shape Safari — Summative Rubric
summative_rubric.purpose: Used during and after Lesson 5 (Shape Safari Art Capstone) to score each child against six expectations on a 4-level scale. Aligned with Ontario Kindergarten Communication of Learning conventions: descriptive, observational, growth-oriented.

levels.descriptor: With significant adult prompting, names 1-2 2D shapes only some of the time. Does not yet describe properties.
Names 3-4 2D shapes most of the time with prompts. Describes basic properties (round vs straight) when asked.
Independently names 5 2D shapes (circle, triangle, square, rectangle, hexagon) and describes properties using shape vocabulary.
Names additional 2D shapes (oval, pentagon, semicircle) beyond the core 5 and spontaneously identifies 2D shapes in the environment.
Cannot consistently distinguish 2D from 3D. May call all shapes 'shapes' without flat/solid distinction.
Names 1-2 3D shapes (typically cube and sphere). Recognizes 3D as 'solid' when prompted.
Independently names 5 3D shapes (sphere, cube, cylinder, cone, pyramid) and clearly distinguishes 2D from 3D using flat/solid vocabulary.
Articulates faces, edges, and vertices for 3D shapes and recognizes that 3D shapes have 2D faces (e.g., 'a cube's face is a square').

rows.expectation_text: use positional language (above, below, beside, inside, outside)

levels.descriptor: Uses 1-2 position words (typically 'in' and 'on') for everything. Does not yet differentiate above/below or inside/outside reliably.
Uses 3-4 position words with prompts. May still confuse above with below or inside with between.
Independently uses 5+ position words (above, below, beside, inside, outside) accurately to describe object placement.
Combines two position words ('above and beside') and applies position vocabulary spontaneously across the day.
Stacks pattern blocks randomly without a target. Cannot identify when a bigger shape can be made from smaller ones.
Composes a square from 2 triangles or a hexagon from 6 triangles with adult prompts. Decomposing remains difficult.
Independently composes target shapes (square, hexagon, rectangle, house) from pattern blocks AND decomposes a bigger shape into smaller named shapes.
Composes the same target shape two different ways (e.g., hexagon = 6 triangles OR 2 trapezoids) and explains why both work.
Stacks 3D shapes randomly without a target. Cannot name the shapes used in a structure.
Builds a simple structure (tower from cubes) and names 1-2 of the 3D shapes used.
Independently builds a multi-shape 3D structure (bridge, house, tower) AND names which 3D shapes were used.
Builds a structure using all 5 different 3D shapes AND describes the structure using position words ('the cone is above the cube').
Describes location only with pointing or 'here'/'there'. Cannot articulate position relationships in words.
Describes object location with 1-2 position words when prompted. Often confuses similar pairs (above/below).
Independently describes object location using full 'The ___ is ___ the ___' sentence frame with correct position words.
Produces multi-clause descriptions ('the lion is above the rocks AND beside the tree') and uses position words across the school day spontaneously.

rows.expectation_text: use shapes in art and patterns

levels.descriptor: Free-draws without using identifiable shapes. Cannot name shapes in their own artwork.
Includes 2-3 shapes in their artwork with prompts. Can name some of the shapes when pointed to.
Independently uses 5+ different shapes in a safari picture, composes at least one bigger shape from smaller ones, and labels the shapes used.
Mixes 2D and 3D representations in artwork, includes a composed shape with multiple sub-shapes, and describes the picture using position words.

summative_rubric.usage_notes: Score during the Lesson 5 capstone phases (mostly visible from the worksheet artifact) and confirm during the gallery walk (partner observation). Level 3 is the grade-level expectation; aim for most children to land at L2 or L3 by end-of-unit. L1 is a signal for additional support; L4 is a signal for enrichment in Grade 1. Communicate scores to families using the Communication of Learning narrative format ('demonstrates a developing understanding of...') rather than letter grades.
summative_rubric.layout_description: One letter page, landscape orientation, with a 6×4 grid table (6 expectation rows × 4 level columns) plus a left-most column for the expectation code and text. Each cell contains the level descriptor in K-readable type. Title at the top of the page; usage notes printed below the table. Total table approximately 10in wide × 7in tall.

summative_task_script.title: Shape Safari Art Capstone — Summative Administration Guide
summative_task_script.purpose: Ties the Lesson 5 worksheet, the lesson plan's structured capstone phases (Plan-Build-Describe-Share), and the rubric together. Tells the teacher exactly what evidence to look for during each phase and which expectation each phase's evidence maps to.
administration_steps: Before the lesson: photocopy one Safari Capstone template per child plus 5 extras for revisions. Print one rubric per child or maintain a single class rubric on a clipboard with student-name rows pre-filled. Have the Junior Shape Explorer certificates printed and ready for the closing ceremony (do not show them to children before they have earned them).

Phase 1 (Plan, 5 min): Children list 5 shapes in the plan slots. This produces visible evidence for A9.1 and A9.2 (which shapes can the child name). Walk the room and check that each child has identified 5 shapes; nudge children who have left slots blank.

Phase 2 (Build, 12 min): Children draw the safari picture using their planned shapes, including at least 1 composed bigger shape. This produces visible evidence for A9.4 (compose) and A9.7 (shapes in art). Begin one-on-one rubric conferences during this phase — ask each child 'What shape did you compose? What smaller shapes did you use?'.

Phase 3 (Describe, 5 min): Children write 3 sentences using position words. This produces visible evidence for A9.3 and A9.6. Continue rubric conferences. By the end of Phase 3, you should have scored most children on at least 4 of 6 expectations.

Phase 4 (Share, 5 min): Children pair up and walk through their picture with a partner. Listen for partners articulating shape names AND position words AND composed shapes. Use this phase to confirm scores you were uncertain about and to upgrade scores where a child demonstrates Level 4 thinking aloud.

After the lesson: review the rubric with the worksheet artifact in front of you. For any child below Level 3 on any expectation, note what evidence (or absence) drove that decision. Use this for the Communication of Learning narrative.
summative_task_script.scoring_guidance: Use the worksheet artifact as primary evidence and the partner-share conversation as confirming evidence. For each expectation, ask: 'What level of independence and confidence did this child show?' Level 3 is the grade-level goal — aim for most children to land at L2 or L3. Children who are L4 on every expectation are ready for Grade 1 spatial work; document this for the receiving teacher. Children who are L1 on multiple expectations need targeted small-group work in the next math block — do not retain them in K spatial sense; instead build the bridge in concrete play and revisit.

evidence_per_expectation.A9.1: Look at Part 1 (plan list). Did the child list 5+ shapes including 2D shapes (circle, triangle, square, rectangle, hexagon)? Combined with Part 2 (the picture). A child whose plan includes 5+ valid 2D shapes is at Level 3 on A9.1.
evidence_per_expectation.A9.2: Look at Part 1 (plan list). Did the child include any 3D shapes (sphere, cube, cylinder, cone, pyramid)? A child whose plan and picture mix 2D and 3D is at Level 3 on A9.2; only 2D = Level 2.
evidence_per_expectation.A9.3: Look at Part 3 (3 position-word sentences). Does the child use 3 different position words correctly? A child who uses 3 distinct words is at Level 3; one or two repeated words suggests Level 2.
evidence_per_expectation.A9.4: Look at Part 2 (the picture). Did the child compose at least 1 bigger shape from smaller shapes? A composed shape with clear sub-shape outlines is Level 3; multiple composed shapes or composing the same shape two different ways is Level 4.
evidence_per_expectation.A9.5: Lesson 5 doesn't require a 3D structure in the worksheet, but the partner-share may reveal A9.5. If a child describes a 3D structure in their picture (e.g., 'a cube hut'), credit Level 3.
evidence_per_expectation.A9.6: Look at Part 3 (3 sentence frames). A child who completes all 3 sentence frames using the structure 'The ___ is ___ the ___' with correct position words for their own picture is at Level 3.
evidence_per_expectation.A9.7: Look at Part 2 (the picture). Did the child use shapes intentionally to make a recognizable safari scene? A picture with 5+ shapes integrated into recognizable elements is Level 3.

certificate.title: Junior Shape Explorer Certificate
certificate.recipient_field_label: This certificate is proudly presented to:
certificate.achievement_text: For successfully completing the 5-Day Shape Safari unit and demonstrating the skills of a Shape Explorer. A safari shape certificate. Sammy the Safari Sloth congratulates the student.
skills_demonstrated: Using position words to describe location
Building 3D structures and using shapes in art
certificate.layout_description: One letter page, portrait orientation. Decorative ornamental border around the entire page (~0.5in margin). Title 'Junior Shape Explorer Certificate' at the top in large ornate font (~1in tall). Below: the recipient label and a wide blank line for the child's name. Below: 'For successfully completing the 5-Day Shape Safari unit and demonstrating the skills of a Shape Explorer.' Below: a bullet list of the four skills demonstrated. Toward the bottom: two side-by-side signature lines labelled 'Teacher Signature' and 'Date'. At the bottom-centre, a small Sammy the Safari Sloth illustration holding a safari hat. Designed to feel celebratory and ceremonial.
